readings_chosen: Sentence 1: an imperative can be mistaken for a report that an opening happened. I read the quotation as a command, as its grammar states, and keep it wholly mentioned in the bin. The note’s existence is GIVEN; it supplies no asserted opening.

Sentence 2: ‘it’ could otherwise name an object left implicit; I resolve it to the note, the preceding singular object that Ada folds. ‘Folded’ remains fold, with no substitution of hold, press or another shape-book verb. No direction, resistance class, unfolding or result is added. The did and holds clauses on line folding are two program representations of this one happening, not two source claims.

Sentence 3: ‘remained shut’ could be expanded into earlier and later states or into NOT open. I keep the writer’s persistence description as one Fact, remained_shut(gate). No producer is named, so I do not invent a happening or a Result line. Persistence is retained in the free description; no separately timed state is inferred.

Sentences 1–3: note and gate are the kinds named by the text. Ada is recorded only as a thing and doer, without guessing a body response or a more specific kind. Thing lines are GIVEN referents of the asserted clauses. The note’s command alone is not used to assert that an actual gate exists; the gate line points to sentence 3.
